3. Defendant Promila has contested the suit denying the plaintiffs story of settlement and possession is that her husband never settled the suit land in favour of the plaintiff or granted any dakhila or accepted any kabuliat from the plaintiff according to her the kabuliat is collusive and never dated upon and the dakhila forged. The suit land has although been in possession of her husband and since after his death in her possession. It is also her case that the remaining share in the properties was transferred by her husband's two other brothers in favour of one Majibor and others with whom she is in ejmali possession of the land in suit. Her further plea is that without these transferees in possession or record the suit is bad for non-joinder of parties. 

 4. At the trial three witnesses including the contesting parties have been examined on either side. The learned trial court has on consideration of the materials on record held that the plaintiff has failed to prove his story of settlement of the suit land from Sudhir, that the kabuliat is hit by section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, that the plaintiff has failed to prove his possession of the land and that the suit is bad for non-joinder of the transferees from Sunil and Nakul. The plaintiff took an appeal and the learned appellate Judge has agreed in the findings of the trial court on all the points. It is against this decision that the plaintiff has obtained this Rule. 

 8. On the question of defect of parties, it may be noted that the defence case is that the defendant has been possessing her 1/3 share, that is, the land in suit ejmali with her co-sharers who are the transferees from her husband’s two brothers. The courts below have found such possession of the defendant in the land. The suit is for simple declaration of title to the land claimed by the contesting defendant. The plaintiff does not claim any relief against the transferees nor is it impossible to pass an effective decree in the suit in their absence. So they cannot be said to the necessary parties. But it cannot be denied that in the facts and circumstances of the case their presence is a matter of convenience to enable the court to adjudicate upon and settle all questions involved in the suit more effectively and completely. Thus though not necessary parties, the transferees from Sunil and Nakul are proper parties in the suit and in such view of the matter, there is no error in the finding of the courts below that the suit is bad for non-joinder of parties, although it must be pointed out that there is no reason for such suit failing without them on record.
